hypothesis: Worker batch_ready/take_count/purge_expired_pending/earliest_pending_deadline rescan the pending vector every loop iteration (estimate() + SipHash + Arc clone per record, Vec::remove shifts). Running byte/record/deadline/leading-run state maintained at intake/drain/removal makes readiness/expiry O(1) and takes hash-free.
limits: Why no gain: the bulk cell never rescans. The step-2 probe measured exactly 1.0 estimate/record in batch_ready, 1.0 iter/record in take_count, 4.0 cheap deadline-compares/record in purge, 1.0/record in earliest (20k records: 20k/20k/80k/20k). Incrementalism moved per-record work from scan time to intake time without reducing total op count; the take_count SipHash->linear saving was offset by intake folds and drain adjusts. Net: +0.11%.

The design would only win where records are scanned K>1 times (linger>0 / slow-fire / deep-backlog workloads with repeated readiness polls). Bulk (linger 0, immediate fires) does not exercise that; a future card could target a linger-heavy cell, but this card's named cell and bar are bulk-only.
